issue.title: [cashubtc/cdk#1487] Report: Unauthenticated CreateBackup RPC allows full database exfiltration
issue.body:
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Severity** | critical |
| **Target** | cashubtc/cdk |
| **Status** | theoretical |
| **Source PR** | [cashubtc/cdk#1487](https://github.com/cashubtc/cdk/pull/1487) |

## Summary

The new `CreateBackup` management RPC endpoint introduced in this PR streams the complete mint database to any caller who presents the correct protocol version header (`x-cdk-protocol-version: 1.0.0`). When the RPC server starts without a TLS directory (the default warned-about insecure mode), no authentication of any kind is enforced. The database contains all proof secrets (Y-values identifying spent ecash tokens), Lightning payment preimages from completed melt operations, all quote records, blind signatures, and full transaction history. Any attacker who can reach the RPC port — whether through a misconfigured firewall, a shared hosting environment, or a local network — can exfiltrate the entire database in a single streaming call.
